claims.text: Large language models are systematically more confident when providing reasoning before answering multiple-choice questions.
The increase in confidence from reasoning before answering is larger when the selected answer is incorrect than when it is correct.
The reasoning process alters token probabilities because final answer prediction depends jointly on the question and self-generated reasoning.
Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting degrades calibration by increasing the proportion of high-confidence wrong answers.

evidence.description: Experiments on a general knowledge benchmark covering 57 subjects and seven LLMs demonstrated systematically higher confidence when reasoning prior to answering.
Experimental metrics showed a larger delta in confidence for incorrect responses compared to correct ones under reasoning conditions.
Hypothesized mechanism explaining inflated confidence estimates based on joint dependencies between question text and model-generated intermediate reasoning tokens.
Evaluations using Expected Calibration Error and Brier score revealed degraded calibration performance under CoT prompting.

methodologies.name: MCQ Confidence and Calibration Analysis under CoT
methodologies.description: Compared LLM confidence levels and calibration metrics across direct response and Chain-of-Thought reasoning approaches.
